scenario.title: May 2024 Solar Storm
scenario.description: A seven-day ARES-6 training campaign featuring a historical NASA solar-storm case study on Mars day 4.
scenario.historicalScope: The May 20, 2024 event is historical. The other six daily events remain part of the ARES-6 educational simulation and are not a replay of Curiosity's actual mission days.

events.title: Let's prepare the food garden!
events.description: Your crew has arrived on Mars. Should you plant the first crops now, or save power and water for other jobs?
events.scienceFact: Plants need water, light, and nutrients — the things that help them grow. A greenhouse gives plants a place with the right conditions.

choices.label: Plant the first crops
choices.description: Spend 5 power units and 5 water units to plant food. The crops need two Mars days to grow.
choices.explanation: Your crops are growing. They need time before they are ready to harvest.

choices.label: Save power and water
choices.description: Keep your supplies for other important jobs around the outpost.
choices.explanation: You saved your supplies, but no food is growing in the greenhouse yet.

events.title: Dust is covering our solar panels!
events.description: A dust storm has left dust on the solar panels. Dusty panels make less electricity for the outpost.
events.scienceFact: Mars can have huge dust storms. Dust on a solar panel can block sunlight, so the panel makes less electricity.

choices.label: Clean the solar panels
choices.description: Spend 5 power units to clean the panels. They can make more electricity again.
choices.explanation: The panels are clean. They can now make more electricity each Mars day.

choices.label: Keep our power
choices.description: Save your electricity for other important equipment.
choices.explanation: You kept your power, but the dusty panels will keep making less electricity.

events.title: The robot rover found an interesting rock!
events.description: Your robot rover has found a rock that scientists would like to study. You can collect a sample or save power.
events.scienceFact: By studying Martian rocks, scientists learn how Mars changed over time and what the planet was like long ago.

choices.label: Collect a rock sample
choices.description: Spend 8 power units to study the rock and finish this science goal.
choices.explanation: Great work! Your crew has finished its rock research.

choices.label: Save our power
choices.description: Wait before studying the rock and keep the electricity for later.
choices.explanation: You saved power, but the rock research is not finished.

events.title: A powerful solar storm is reaching Mars!
events.description: Mission Control has received news of a major solar storm. Charged particles have reached Mars. Should your crew use extra shelter protection or save the water?
events.scienceFact: The Sun can send bursts of energy and tiny charged particles into space. When a strong burst reaches Mars, it can increase radiation at the surface.

choices.label: Move the crew into the radiation shelter
choices.description: Set aside 5 water units to add basic shelter protection. In this game, it lowers the radiation-risk points from this event.
choices.explanation: The crew has extra shelter protection. It lowers the game's radiation-risk points, not a real measured dose.

choices.label: Save the water
choices.description: Keep the water for the crew's normal needs. The shelter will not have extra protection for this event.
choices.explanation: You kept the water, but the crew has no extra shelter protection for this event.

historicalRecord.radFinding: Curiosity's Radiation Assessment Detector recorded the biggest radiation surge of its mission since the rover landed in 2012.
historicalRecord.doseExplanation: NASA estimated that astronauts standing near Curiosity during this event could have received about 8,100 microgray (8.1 milligray) — around 30 chest X-rays.
historicalRecord.scienceNote: This is NASA's estimate of a possible astronaut dose near Curiosity during the historical event. It is not a measurement of the ARES-6 crew and is not used as a game damage value.
historicalRecord.gameModelNote: ARES-6 uses a simple danger level and fictional risk points for this choice. The shelter option lowers those game points; it does not calculate a real astronaut dose.
historicalRecord.sourceTitle: NASA: Watches Mars Light Up During Epic Solar Storm

events.title: The habitat's air system has stopped!
events.description: The machine that keeps the habitat's air safe is not working. Fix it now, or use backup mode for one Mars day.
events.scienceFact: People need clean air to breathe. A Mars home needs machines to provide and manage safe air for the crew.

choices.label: Fix the air system
choices.description: Spend 6 power units to repair the machine that keeps the habitat's air safe.
choices.explanation: The air system is working again. The crew can breathe safely inside the habitat.

choices.label: Use backup mode
choices.description: Save power for now. The air system will still need to be fixed by the next Mars day.
choices.explanation: Backup mode gives the crew a little time. Fix the air system before another Mars day passes.

events.title: Should we grow more food?
events.description: The crew can start another crop cycle or save supplies. If the habitat's air system is still broken, fixing it is also important.
events.scienceFact: Growing food on Mars takes planning. Plants need water, power, light, and time before they are ready to harvest.

choices.label: Fix the air system
choices.description: Spend 6 power units to restore the habitat's air system.
choices.explanation: You repaired the habitat. The crew can use its air system again.

choices.label: Grow another batch of food
choices.description: Spend 5 power units and 5 water units to start another crop cycle. The crops need two Mars days to grow.
choices.explanation: New crops are growing. They need two Mars days before harvest. Make sure the air system is working too.

events.title: One last science mission!
events.description: Before the seven-day mission ends, your crew has one last chance to study the land and conditions around the outpost.
events.scienceFact: Scientists study Mars's air, weather, soil, and radiation to understand what future explorers may face.

choices.label: Study Mars's environment
choices.description: Spend 8 power units to finish this science goal.
choices.explanation: Excellent work! Your crew has finished its study of the Martian environment.

choices.label: Save our remaining power
choices.description: Keep your electricity for the outpost instead of doing the final study.
choices.explanation: You saved power, but the study of Mars's environment is not finished.
